title: Your CPU runs code that may never happen
body: To keep its pipeline full, a modern CPU guesses which way each branch goes and executes ahead speculatively. A wrong guess flushes that work, costing a dozen or more cycles. Predictable patterns run measurably faster than random ones with identical instruction counts, which is why sorted data can speed up a simple loop.
source_hint: Intel / AMD optimisation manuals on branch prediction
